top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn; B001) is a measurement advance with a clean credit boundary. Demand estimation with endogenous prices, built on Berry's inversion and the jointly authored 1995 BLP paper, recovers substitution patterns, markups and welfare counterfactuals that reduced-form work could not. It has about three decades of use and critique, has been applied in merger review and regulation, and has spread into trade, health and environmental economics. The documented sensitivities to numerics, instruments and functional form qualify the method but do not undermine the core result, and the citation should avoid overclaiming precision. Leaving out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin is a real cost of the three-name cap. A method-level citation can be defended, and it avoids splitting the jointly authored central result. My own first choice in round 1 was B013. I moved away from it because its credit boundary (Katz versus Dorn) and the magnitudes of the China-shock effects are less settled than B001's. Award is clearly preferable to no award (P000), since the work is mature, original and consequential.
